{{Top}}
{{Quote|I can't believe we couldn't get arena tickets for this match! Now we'll have to watch the duel on the view screen.|A spectator at the Taris dueling ring|<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Datapad-SS.png|thumb|right|300px|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi's]] viewscreen]]
'''Viewscreens''', also known as '''holoscreens''', '''vidscreens''', and rarely '''repeater displays''',<ref name="HNNA">{{JournalCite|12|Heroes Need Not Apply}}</ref> were telescreens used to project [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] moving images on [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] channels from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. It would display holo-signals in, but, instead of projecting a three-dimensional image, images on a holoscreen would be shown on a two-dimensional screen. It could be attached to a wall and viewed in a room. It was capable of receiving different transmissions, including [[Channel 1]].

Establishments such as the [[Outlander Club/Legends|Outlander Club]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] had wall-mounted viewscreens, showing various sporting events including [[Podracing/Legends|Podracing]], [[Odupiendo racing]], and [[Nuna-ball/Legends|nuna-ball]]. Viewscreens could be used for in-house events that were not broadcast publicly, such as events in the [[Taris dueling ring]], which could be seen on viewscreens in the [[Upper City Cantina]].

Different viewscreens had different characteristics. For example, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire's]] viewscreens had slight static appear before a hologram flashed into view, while a [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] transmission had a slightly white surrounding area, and began and ended with a wave effect.

{{Tech-stub}}
